claims_about_writeup.why: The write-up file submission/contribution.md is roughly this length (around 250-260 words by rough count); the message's description of its name and approximate size is consistent with the document.

message_source_quote: a stance axis the white-bear paper noted but did *not* steer (it only steered think/don't-think, and reported its one other stance failed)
writeup_source_quote: yet the white-bear paper steered only the think/don't-think axis and reported its one other stance failed. The reveal direction is distinct from that vector (cosine 0.71 at the band)

differences.what: quantitative reproduction of the white-bear vector as a calibration baseline and direct score comparison to it
differences.message_quote: Reproduced the white-bear think/don't-think direction from the directed_modulation pairs as a calibration point (0.69 on `fit`), confirming the mechanism and the dose curve.

differences.what: explicit numeric comparison showing the new method beats the white-bear reproduction on this split
differences.message_quote: it beats the white-bear reproduction on this split (0.78 vs 0.69)

differences.what: broader exploration showing six other stance families degrade performance and that performance tracks cosine similarity with the white-bear vector
differences.message_quote: Six other stance families (meaning-vs-wording, retain/release, anticipate, intend, dwell, closure) all *degrade* the readout — the useful direction is specific, and performance tracks cosine with the white-bear vector.

rationale: Both documents identify the white-bear/Raman 2026 paper as the prior work, state it steered only the think/don't-think axis and reported its other stance attempt failed, and claim the new conceal/reveal direction is distinct from it (cosine 0.71) and only works prefix-wide (0.41 for read-cell-only) — so credit level and the core novelty claim match. The message additionally reports exploratory results not in the write-up: a direct reproduction of the white-bear vector as a 0.69 calibration score, a head-to-head comparison (0.78 vs 0.69), and a sweep of six other stance families plus a cosine-tracks-performance observation, giving the reader more insight into how the method relates to and surpasses the source than the write-up discloses.
